name: Treaty with the Wea, 1820
aka: Treaty of Vincennes with the Wea, August 11, 1820
nations: Wea (now part of the Peoria Tribe of Indians of Oklahoma)
promises: $5,000 in money and goods for the Wabash reservation kept under the 1818 treaty (Article 2).
The Wea annuity under the 1818 treaty would be paid at Kaskaskia, Illinois, after their move (Article 3).

breaches.what: The Wea claimed before the Indian Claims Commission that $5,000, about 18 cents an acre, was not a fair or conscionable price for the 27,330.66-acre reservation ceded by this treaty. The parties settled for a net final judgment of $33,262.92, approved by the Peoria Tribe's Business Committee, without a ruling on the merits.

landTaken: Royce Area 114, the Wea reservation on the Wabash in Indiana, 27,330.66 acres by the Bureau of Land Management's survey plats (Docket 314-E findings, 1967).
compensation: $5,000 in money and goods, about 18 cents an acre. Settlement judgment of $33,262.92 in 1967.
today: The Wea united with the Piankeshaw, Peoria and Kaskaskia in 1849; the formal consolidation of the four tribes was effected by the treaty of 30 May 1854, and their claims are carried by the Peoria Tribe of Indians of Oklahoma (Docket 314-E findings).

nationVoice.nation: Peoria Tribe of Indians of Oklahoma
nationVoice.summary: The Tribe's history says the Wea gave up their remaining Indiana reserve in the treaty of August 1820 and, having disposed of all their lands, moved to Missouri and Arkansas to join the other tribal members and the Piankashaw.

openQuestions: The settlement made no finding that the price was unconscionable, so this treaty is shown as contested, not broken.
A Peoria Tribe statement on this treaty was not found.
Audit 2026-11-08: 'today' said the 1849 union was 'formally recognized' by the 1854 treaty; the Commission's words are that the formal consolidation was effected by it, so the sentence now says that.
